findings.problem: left_inv and right_inv are the same argument with T and S swapped. Each one changes the goal to an equiv-snd statement, then uses equiv_snd_eq_iff_rightCosetEquivalence together with changeRep_rightCoset to replace the argument by the original representative. It then closes with equiv_snd_eq_self_of_mem_of_one_mem. Any fix to this round-trip argument has to be made twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Inside `section Representatives` (T explicit, H fixed), add before `changeRepEquiv`:

lemma changeRep_changeRep (S : H.RightTransversal) (t : ↥(T : Set G)) :
    changeRep S T (changeRep T S t) = t := by
  change (T.2.equiv (changeRep T S t : G)).2 = t
  calc
    _ = (T.2.equiv (t : G)).2 :=
      T.2.equiv_snd_eq_iff_rightCosetEquivalence.2 (changeRep_rightCoset T S t)
    _ = t := T.2.equiv_snd_eq_self_of_mem_of_one_mem H.one_mem t.2

Then use it twice under the same hypotheses:
  left_inv t := changeRep_changeRep T S t
  right_inv s := changeRep_changeRep S T s

The second use is the lemma with the roles of T and S exchanged. Both hypotheses are over the same H, so it typechecks. The proof body is the existing left_inv proof. It may need a minor coercion or defeq adjustment, since I could not compile it.
findings.benefit: The round-trip argument is stated and proved once, with a named lemma (`changeRep_changeRep`) that is also useful as a simp or rewrite fact. `changeRepEquiv` becomes two one-line fields, and the symmetry between T and S is explicit instead of being visible only by comparing two blocks.
